title: IsoScore: Measuring the Uniformity of Embedding Space Utilization
alt: Three two-dimensional point clouds, from a roughly circular cloud on the left to an increasingly narrow ellipse on the right.
caption: IsoScore, Figure 3. Gaussian samples with covariance diag(x, 1), where x = 1, 3, and 75 from left to right.
context: The three point clouds occupy the same two-dimensional space. Their shapes differ because variance becomes increasingly concentrated along one axis.
question: What are the implications of the middle panel's shape on dimensional utilization?
answer: The middle cloud uses about 1.61 dimensions under the paper’s dimension-use heuristic. It spreads along both axes, but unequally. This estimate describes how uniformly the space is used; the ambient space is still two-dimensional.
evidence_summary: Section 4.2 interprets the middle case as using between one and two dimensions. The estimate comes from the paper’s definition of dimension use.
source_label: Rudman et al. (2022), Figure 3 and Section 4.2
provenance: Question from this site’s MQUD example 34. Caption, context, and explanation adapted from the IsoScore paper.
